tldr: ACP lets an AI agent run checkout against a merchant's own API: it creates and updates a session, gets a payment token scoped to that merchant and amount, and completes the order, while the merchant stays merchant of record.
whyItExists: Shopping inside a chat window needs a way for the AI surface to build a cart, show authoritative prices and taxes, and pay without becoming the store. Card forms and redirects break the conversation, and handing raw card numbers to every merchant's API is unsafe. ACP gives the merchant a small REST contract it hosts itself, lets a payment provider swap the card for a single-use token limited by an allowance, and leaves orders, payments, refunds and chargebacks with the merchant.

whatItIsNot.text: Not IBM's Agent Communication Protocol, not Virtuals' Agent Commerce Protocol, not ERC-8183 and not the Agent Client Protocol. The PyPI package acp-sdk is IBM's.
OpenAI is not the merchant of record. The merchant is, its name appears on the card statement, and it handles refunds and chargebacks.
The Shared Payment Token is Stripe's product used with ACP, not the ACP specification. The spec defines a generic Delegate Payment endpoint; spt is only an example credential type.

Not the 2025 Instant Checkout any more, and not ChatGPT Wallet. OpenAI scaled back in-chat checkout in March 2026, and ChatGPT uses ACP mainly for product feeds and discovery, with merchants on their own checkout. ChatGPT Wallet (2026-11-13) pays on the merchant's existing checkout with a payment token that OpenAI's post says the payment network provides, not one from ACP Delegate Payment or a Stripe SPT, and OpenAI does not present it as ACP.
Not a mandate protocol. ACP has no signed proof of user intent like AP2's mandates; the allowance limits what a token can do, not why.
Not versioned by releases. Versions are dated spec folders with no GitHub release or tag, and released folders were edited after release.
Not bridged to UCP. The two share several status names and a well-known discovery pattern, but no mapping or bridge specification exists.

changedRecently.text: A community security review (issue 331, not an advisory) says ACP's agent-to-merchant request signing is weakest on Delegate Payment: the Delegate Authentication RFC lists the Signature header as required and says it must be verified, the Delegate Payment RFC lists it as recommended although its request rules say the client must sign, and the discovery RFC defers signing-key advertisement. No maintainer had responded by 2026-11-21.

OpenAI announced ChatGPT Wallet, rolling out first in dots for US ChatGPT Pro subscribers. It pays with a network token on the merchant's existing checkout, and OpenAI does not present it as ACP. As read 2026-11-21, the post names American Express, Chase, Mastercard and Visa as partners, with Chase taking part as a card issuer, where launch-day coverage named three; OpenAI's help article limits Wallet to conversations with a dot.

Between 2026-11-12 and 2026-11-13 OpenAI rewrote its developer commerce docs into the Commerce in ChatGPT Partner Playbook, which no longer describes ACP, Instant Checkout or delegated payment; the old ACP pages redirect or answer 404.

OpenAI introduced Businesses in ChatGPT in beta. Since the 2026-11-13 docs rewrite, OpenAI's developer docs send businesses to Business Hub to claim a profile, verify their identity and upload full product feed snapshots, replacing the approved-partner form. Its Business Agents, which a business can create only after Persona identity verification, explain products and link to the business's website but cannot complete purchases.

OpenAI's merchant page, as read that day and again on 2026-11-21, says there are no fees for purchases made on the merchant's site or app, and its FAQ says purchases that start in ChatGPT carry no fees. It still says ChatGPT shopping is built on ACP; applicants wait on a waitlist, and a self-serve merchant platform is planned.

In ChatGPT plugins (formerly the Apps SDK), external checkout is generally available, with approval limited to physical goods. A plugin may show payment methods already saved with the merchant, and the payment sheet is a private beta for select marketplace partners (unchanged on 2026-11-21).

A dispute-resolution extension SEP (PR 316) was filed and awaits a sponsor; a comment marked it ready for maintainer review on 2026-11-06, and it had no maintainer reply by 2026-11-21, after a new commit on 2026-11-16 and a 2026-11-18 request to Meta's TSC representative to sponsor it. Issue 315 (2026-10-15) asks for stored agent identity.

Last commit so far: an optional product url on checkout items (unreleased). No commit, tag or release landed between then and 2026-11-21, and no maintainer commented, reviewed or merged in that window.
The released 2026-04-17 order schema was edited after release; its status list now says completed where the changelog says delivered.
Meta joined the Technical Steering Committee as seat 3.
Version 2026-04-17 released: Cart, a push Feed API, Delegate Authentication (3DS2), /.well-known/acp.json discovery, the MCP binding and a mandatory Idempotency-Key on every POST.
